purpose: Decorative cover artwork. Interactive technical diagrams remain code-rendered.

prompts.subject: Electronics fundamentals: a carefully arranged macro still life of a blue electrolytic capacitor, three axial striped resistors with bent silver leads, an unlit clear red LED, a small black transistor and a premium handheld digital multimeter with red and black leads. Loose components on a warm cream work mat; no assembled circuit board, no laptop.

Circuit Lab: a white solderless breadboard with one bright golden lit LED, an axial resistor and carefully routed short red and dark teal jumper wires, powered by a small 9V battery. A green circuit board with copper traces sits partly behind it. Focus on building, working connections and the glowing light. No multimeter, no loose scattered parts.

Auto Mechanics: a convincing professionally machined single-cylinder four-stroke engine educational cutaway displayed on a workbench. Curved cast aluminum cooling fins and cylinder head, exposed polished piston and ring grooves inside the bore, one slender connecting rod linked to a steel crankshaft below, two overhead poppet valves and a ceramic spark plug above. Recognizable real engine proportions and material detail, warm light inside the cutaway, a small socket wrench nearby. Avoid toy cubes, arbitrary gears or impossible clusters of rods. A decorative cover illustration, not a labeled diagram.

Game Lab: a premium slim modern laptop showing a polished colorful contemporary 3D garage adventure game, a cheerful little mechanic robot collecting a golden wrench among rubber tires in a miniature garage. A small wireless game controller in the foreground. The screen shows the game world only, no code. Modern smooth cinematic graphics, not pixel art, no retro arcade.

Faith and Trail: an open well-used Bible with cream pages, a brass compass on a folded topographic map and a neatly coiled small length of outdoor rope, on a weathered wooden trail table. Soft pine forest and distant mountain ridge blurred behind. Gentle warm morning sunlight. No human figures, no official logos, no readable printed page text.

Coding workshop: a modern slim laptop on a tidy desk, screen split between an elegant dark code editor with colorful abstract code lines and a bright modern web page preview with cards, a mountain photograph and a large green button. A small miniature website window floats just above the screen as a creative dimensional detail. No game character, no controller, no blocky pixel styling, no readable text.
